what: MEMORY_CONSOLIDATE run on main: reviewed all 42 decisions.jsonl entries (EP-1 through EP-31) for promotable facts not already captured in knowledge/*.md. what: EP-32: fixed a live update-path bug the user hit testing UPDATE_PROMPT.md -- an ad-hoc task file with no matching branch got orphan-swept and archived despite EP-29's fix. Root cause was two-layered: MIGRATIONS.md's v2.1.0 orphan-sweep bullet predated EP-29's ad-hoc-name exception and was never updated, and ai_os_version was never bumped past 2.1.1 despite EP-28/29/30/31 shipping real behavior changes, so UPDATE_PROMPT's version-gated migration walk would have skipped a corrected section anyway. Fixed the stale bullet in place, added a v2.2.0 MIGRATIONS.md section for EP-28/29/30/31 (incl. forcing commands/aliases.json's wrap key even though that file is otherwise preserve-user-customizations), bumped ai_os_version to 2.2.0 in manifest.json and README. Also fixed the same non-main-branch staleness in all 7 bridge/template files (root AGENTS.md, .agents/AGENTS.md, 5 installer templates). Separately fixed UPDATE_PROMPT.md Step 3, which unconditionally overwrote BOOT.md/kernel/rules with zero check -- any KERNEL OVERRIDE AUTHORIZED customization would be silently destroyed on update. Now searches decisions.jsonl/decisions.archive.jsonl/progress.md for KERNEL OVERRIDE entries targeting those files first, and surfaces/offers to re-merge instead of overwriting blind, using the framework's own mandatory kernel-edit logging as the signal since there's no stored baseline to diff against
why: same class of bug as the earlier README staleness catches, but this one caused an actual data-loss-adjacent failure in a live test rather than just a doc mismatch -- confirms installer/updater sync needs to happen inside the same EP that changes kernel behavior, not as a separate later pass. The kernel-overwrite gap is the same risk one level up: even correct migrations don't help if the update blindly clobbers authorized kernel customizations that were never migrations to begin with

what: EP-33: added MEMORY_AMEND to core.memory.sk -- the missing direction in the promotion pipeline. TASK_CLOSE/MEMORY_CONSOLIDATE only add to semantic memory or delete something a new fact supersedes; neither revisits an existing entry just because it was later found wrong (verified REVIEW_CREDIBILITY, HEAL_DIAGNOSE, and Diff-Driven Debugging don't cover this either before concluding it was a real gap). MEMORY_AMEND verifies the challenged claim is actually responsible, then corrects in place (stale fact), relocates to known_gotchas.md (true but harmful advice -- keep the lesson, drop the recommendation), or removes outright (diff-before-delete) -- same archetype-scaled accept gate as any other semantic-memory write. BOOT.md SS7 gained a memory-traced-debugging trigger and SS4 a matching routing callout, applying the EP-31 dataflow-routing lesson proactively this time. Bumped ai_os_version to 2.3.0 and added the MIGRATIONS.md section in the same pass per the EP-32 lesson
why: user asked, after discussing the value of shared semantic memory, whether an entry later found to have caused a bug actually gets amended -- checking confirmed it didn't, a real gap given a bad shared promotion has a bigger blast radius than a private mistake
